content.text: I've measured 4 of the 5 EQE points; the highest so far is index 3 (Sb 0.19). Before I spend the last one, I'm running XRD on nearby compositions to see where the phase changes.

input.rationale: Across 5 EQE measurements, the highest EQE was at index 3 (Sb 0.19): 0.098%. Neighbours were lower: Sb 0.12 gave 0.063%, Sb 0.23 gave 0.073%, Sb 0.46 gave 0.016% and Sb 0.71 gave 0.005%. So EQE peaks sharply on the Fe-rich side, around Sb ≈ 0.19. XRD at Sb 0.19, 0.25 and 0.33 gave the same peak set (Q 1.878, 2.37, 2.65, 3.56 1/Å). That suggests one crystalline phase across this range, possibly a rutile-type Fe–Sb oxide, though I did not confirm this against reference patterns. The trend therefore appears to come from composition or defect effects, not a phase change.

content.text:
I've submitted **index 3 (Sb fraction 0.19)** as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.098%, the highest of the five I measured. That uses the whole EQE budget; I used 3 of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.12 | 0.063 |
| **3** | **0.19** | **0.098** |
| 5 | 0.23 | 0.073 |
| 13 | 0.46 | 0.016 |
| 22 | 0.71 | 0.005 |

- **Trend:** EQE is highest on the Fe-rich end and drops steadily as Sb increases. Around Sb 0.46, near the FeSbO₄ composition, it is already about six times lower than the best.
- **Structure:** XRD at Sb 0.19, 0.25 and 0.33 showed the same set of peaks, so the crystal structure looks unchanged across that range. The drop in EQE therefore seems to come from composition itself, not a switch to a different phase. I didn't check these peaks against reference patterns, so I can't say which phase it is.
- **Uncertainty:** The peak is narrow, and the nearest measured points (Sb 0.12 and 0.23) are both clearly lower. Indices 1, 2 and 4 (Sb 0.14–0.21) were never measured and could beat index 3.
